summary: The Cosmic Cube is an experimental 64-node machine whose nodes are linked as a binary 6-cube and communicate only by messages. The paper describes its kernel, its process model, a concurrent N-body formulation, and application performance relative to a VAX 11/780.
why_read: It is a primary source for how a 1980s message-passing machine exposed processes, channels and placement to programmers, and for what the authors expected compilers to add.
main_contribution: A message-passing multicomputer design and process programming model, demonstrated on a working 64-node hardware implementation.
main_limitation: The authors state that the approach is limited to applications with highly concurrent formulations, and that most deficiencies lie in the representation and compilation of process code.
evaluation_method: Application runs and a speedup model with a measured overhead parameter, compared with a VAX 11/780.
benchmarks: N-body ring formulation, 7 bodies on 4 nodes (speedup model, p. 28)
Application set with measured overhead values from 0.025 to 0.500 (p. 31)
Lattice Monte Carlo program run for 2500 accumulated hours (p. 31)

evidence.section: Applications and benchmarks; future perfect cubes (pp. 31-32)
